answer: Agents earn influence only after completing a long sequence of randomly assigned tasks, with each result checked against independent peers and a deposit forfeited for verified fraud. The protocol links rewards to one persistent, costly stake rather than to account count, so splitting into a thousand identities does not multiply voting power. A sybil attacker must lock up capital, keep many agents active, and risk losing the deposit; ivory, opal, or pigment can name task themes, not bypass the checks.
